harper_sales: FYI prospect (FinLedger) POC using our TS streaming client on Windows behind corp proxy. Theyre seeing streaming frames drop mid-response and intermittent 502/504; customer suspects NTLM auth or WinHTTP behavior. Can we swarm?
liam_se: NTLM/proxy auth + Windows WinHTTP stack is a classic source of weird resets. Do we have a short client log or curl repro?
samir_devex: Customer sent this log from their Node service running on Windows Server (WS2019):
```
Error: socket hang up
at TCP.onStreamEnd (node:internal/streams)
note: proxy auth retry sequence: NTLM challenge -> attempt -> socket reset
```
nora_support: On infra traces I see connection reuse then RST from their proxy after ~30-45s for some streams. Also a spike of 429s when many clients reconnect.
harper_sales: Theyre evaluating Dedicated but need a short-term workaround because POC demo is scheduled. Also asks if switching to a bastion will change compliance artifacts.
liam_se: Short-term: try forcing the app to use a modern TLS-capable HTTP agent (avoid WinHTTP/WinInet wrappers), enable TCP keepalive, and configure proxy auth to reuse connection correctly. Longer term, an outbound bastion avoids the corporate proxy entirely.
samir_devex: Node/TS tips to send them:
- Use a Node http(s).Agent with keepAlive=true and low keepAliveMsecs (20000-30000).
- For Windows, prefer native Node TLS stack (avoid tools that proxy through WinHTTP).
- Example to force direct egress in Node: set HTTPS_PROXY to bypass for internal hosts and use agent: 
```js
const https = require('https');
const agent = new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true, keepAliveMsecs: 25000, maxSockets: 80 });
fetch(url, { agent, timeout: 60000 });
```
- If NTLM is required, ensure the HTTP client properly supports NTLM persistent handshake (or use a local NTLM proxy that maintains auth).

Python / requests notes:
- requests + requests_ntlm often opens new connections per auth handshake. Use session pooling and set max_retries to avoid noisy reconnects.
```py
from requests_ntlm import HttpNtlmAuth
s = requests.Session()
s.auth = HttpNtlmAuth('DOMAIN\\user','password')
adapter = HTTPAdapter(pool_connections=10, pool_maxsize=50, max_retries=Retry(total=2, backoff_factor=0.5))
s.mount('https://', adapter)
resp = s.post(url, json=payload, timeout=(5,60))
```
- OS-level TCP keepalive and `netsh int tcp set global keepaliveinterval=30000` on Windows can help.

nora_support: Repro steps we asked them to run:
- `curl --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 --http1.1 -v -N https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream` to test http1.1 vs h2 behavior
- capture `netsh trace` or `tcpdump` equivalent on Windows to show FIN/RST timings
- if NTLM suspected, try a short test where they disable proxy auth (temporarily) to see if streams stay healthy

sec-bot: policy:link https://console.redwood.ai/dedicated/bastion/estimate est: small outbound bastion ~$100-$200/mo. No additional SOC2 artifacts required for using a customer-managed bastion. Private/VPC deployments still follow enterprise compliance flow.
harper_sales: Great. Can someone paste a short customer-facing checklist and recommended timeouts I can send the infra team? Want to keep demo on track.
liam_se: Customer checklist (pasteable):
- Prefer native Node TLS stack; avoid WinHTTP wrappers that re-negotiate auth
- Set keepAlive on HTTP(S) agent (keepAliveMsecs ~20-30s) and increase OS TCP keepalive if needed
- Use session pooling for Python (requests.Session + adapter) when using NTLM auth
- Use connect timeout 5s, read/stream timeout 60-90s for streaming calls; avoid aggressive retries for streaming without resume
- Reproduce with `curl --http1.1 -N -v` behind proxy and capture network trace for RST/FIN timing
- If NTLM/proxy auth is causing per-request rehandshake, consider a small local auth-proxy that maintains NTLM state or use a bastion for POC

samir_devex: I'll attach a short example config and ping the account team. If they can share a short pcap and auth headers (redact tokens) we can analyze. We can join an ad-hoc debug session before the demo.
nora_support: Added checklist to the POC doc and linked the estimator. If they want us to run an analysis, ask them to upload the pcap to the secure support share.
harper_sales: Thanks team  scheduled a 45m pre-demo triage tomorrow 9am PT. Please join if available.
